title: No case-side document link table or field IDs in the sources
source: TSD P3 v3 T3.1; Ownership Map v1 (case_document_check, document, document_intake all P5); legacy RWB-E1-032 section 11
description: The legacy story wrote the document, the intake item and the decision log entry, all in the document hub. rwb-case has no table that links a case to a stored document, and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 gives no field IDs for such a link. The story needs one row per case and document with a checklist state and the extracted field count.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 lists recovery_case, case_account, case_party, queue, assignment, task, timer, interaction, case_entry_exclusion and the reference and parameter tables; no document link table. Ownership Map: case_document_check owner P5, document owner P5.
proposed: Create rwb_case.case_document_link in this story's migration V1032_1 with case_id, document_id, checklist_state, extracted_field_count, linked_at and source_event_id, a unique key on (case_id, document_id) and no foreign key across services; ask the data steward for the field IDs in the next data dictionary version.

title: No named rwb-source-data operation for the ACE account number
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 (rwb-source-data IN: GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}); API Specification v4 ownership rows; legacy RWB-E1-032 precondition on CaseDirectory.findOpenCasesByAccountNo
description: The matcher passes the ACE account number and rwb-case must resolve it to account_key only through the rwb-source-data contract. The sources name the account resource by identifier but not the filter or query form that carries an account number, and no account lookup path is listed in the API Specification ownership rows.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 and the rwb-source-data contract row give GET /accounts/{id}; the API Specification ownership list for P1 has no /accounts row; the legacy story resolved the account number in process through CaseDirectory.
proposed: Use GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{id} with the ACE account number as the identifier for this story, and agree the query form with rwb-source-data in its contract story before integration.

title: Cadence and time of the daily reconcile Schedule not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 (Temporal Schedules); legacy RWB-E1-032 restart behaviour
description: The case side needs a Schedule that writes the links a timeout left uncreated. The sources fix the mechanism (Temporal Schedule with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window) but not the cadence or the time of day for this run; the legacy story only says a failed attach stays pending for the next run of JOB-12, which is the document hub's job.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 44 job map has no job for a case-side document reconcile; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 12 restart behaviour says items left PENDING are matched in the next run.
proposed: Run the reconcile Schedule daily with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and set the time of day with the operations team before go-live.

title: The rwb-case feature switch key is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-032 section 13 (feature flag rwb.dochub.autoattach); Template and Rules v1 DP-06
description: The legacy feature flag belongs to the document hub. The case-side switch is a parameter read through the parameters contract, but no source names its key or its default.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-032 section 13 names only rwb.dochub.autoattach; the rwb-case parameter catalog in TSD P3 v3 T3.1 has no document parameter.
proposed: Load a rwb-case parameter for the case-side switch through the parameters contract, default on, owned by RW-COE; off means the case side writes nothing from an event.

title: The case review task code and its status values are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-032 AC10 and RWB-E1-054; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 task (DF-WRK-019 task_code, DF-WRK-022 status)
section: 8 Business rules BR5; 9 State transitions; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: A document with review_status PENDING must raise one case review task. No source gives the task code, the element type or the task status values that the case side should write, and the review queue story is a separate slice.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 gives the task fields but no code list for document review; LOV-TASK-STATUS values are not listed for this case; legacy RWB-E1-054 lists review items in the document hub, not as case tasks.
proposed: Hold the task code, element type and status values as reference data in the rwb-case reference tables and load them with RWB-P3-E1043-CON before the review queue story starts.

title: Decision code and final call for the case document link are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-032 AC1 (decision log entry DOCATT); Template and Rules v1 DP-03
description: The case side writes one decision record with the link. The legacy DOCATT entry was written by the document store for the attach; no source gives the decision code or the final call that the case side should use for its own record.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-032 AC1 and BR5 describe the DOCATT entry written by DocumentStore; no decision code is defined for a case-side document link.
proposed: Agree the decision code and the final call with the decision log owner; until then the record names the case, the document and the event id only.

title: Per-service login names for rwb-case and rwb-document are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 DP-02; TSD P3 v3 T6.2 (service identities SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-OCR)
description: The story names the service identities that answer the case-directory reads and that publish the document events. The sources name the service logins by role only and give no login name for rwb-case or rwb-document.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T2.5 and T6.1 name SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES and SY-OCR; no database or service login string is given for either service.
proposed: Name the logins in the platform DB story (one login per service) and reference them here once agreed; the story uses the role names until then.

title: No field IDs for the notice facts on recovery_case, and no event code list for the notice timeline entries
source: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (recovery_case, task, interaction); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 11; Notice resource of RWB-P6-E1052-CON
description: The case side must keep the notice reference, the notice state, the hold reason, the template code and version, the document reference and the delivery date on the case so that the case shows what was generated or held, and it must write one timeline entry per notice request and per delivery. The case table of the module specification has no such column, the data dictionary gives no field ID for them, and no list enumerates the timeline event codes of a notice entry.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 lists recovery_case DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-055 and case_party, task and interaction with no notice column; interaction carries event_code as a LOV-LEDGER-EVENT value whose notice members are not enumerated.
proposed: Create the seven columns in the migration V1052_1 of this story with a unique index on the case and the notice reference and a timeline index, load the notice timeline event codes into LOV-LEDGER-EVENT through the reference-data contract, and ask the data steward for the field IDs in the next data dictionary version.

title: The decision code and the final call of the case-side notice record are only partly specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-052 AC1 and flow step 7 (decision code D7.1, rule R-LIT-03); RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.3; Template and Rules v1 DP-03
section: 8 Business rules BR5; 12.3 Events published; 13 Solution plan
description: The source carries decision code D7.1 for notice generation, written by the service that generates the notice. This story writes a second, case-side record of the same request. No source names the final call or the outcome value that the case-side record should carry, and none says whether the case side reuses D7.1 or takes a code of its own.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-052 flow step 7 and AC1 name D7.1 and R-LIT-03 for the generation entry; RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.3 names the same code for the record of the generating service; no source describes a case-side record of a notice request.
proposed: Reuse decision code D7.1 with the template code and version, the notice reference and the business date, and agree the final call with the decision log owner before build; if the ledger needs one code per writer, agree a case-side code in the rule and decision catalogue.

title: The task model values of the request task and of the task Complete notice data are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-052 AC3 and AC4 (task text Complete notice data); TSD P3 v3 T3.1 task DF-WRK-019 to DF-WRK-026 and T3.2 LOV-ELEMENT, LOV-DISCRETION and LOV-TASK-STATUS
section: 8 Business rules BR3; 9 State transitions; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The case side opens a hold task when the notice is held and completes the request task when the notice is answered. The source gives the task text but no task code for the request task, no element type or discretion for either task and no due date for the hold task. It also does not say whether the hold task is created from the held answer in rwb-case or raised by rwb-comms through the case task operation.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 lists the task fields and T3.2 lists LOV-ELEMENT, LOV-DISCRETION and LOV-TASK-STATUS with no task code for a notice request; the legacy story raises the task inside the generating service.
proposed: Load both task codes, the element type HUMAN_TASK, the discretion REQUIRED and the status values as task rows of the case model through the reference-data contract; create the hold task from the held answer and dedupe a raise that arrives through the case task operation on the same case, task code and business date.

title: Architecture v5 gives P3 as a listener of P6, while the P6 contract accepts a REST notice request
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (connection matrix, P3 row P6 column E), slide 16 note (route services call shared capabilities through Temporal, never through REST), slide 17 (rwb-comms IN: POST /notices); RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.1
section: 4 Flow step 5; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.5 Workflows and activities
description: The story sends the notice request from a rwb-case workflow activity on the rwb-comms contract with one hop and a 2 s timeout. The connection matrix records P3 as listening to P6 only, and the architecture note says route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal and never through REST, while the rwb-comms contract publishes POST /cases/{caseId}/notices as an accepted REST operation.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13 row P3 Case shows E in the P6 column; slide 17 gives P6 the REST request POST /notices and the OUT of P6 as Document, Decision, Integration and ACE Common; RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.1 declares API-P6-001 on the rwb-comms base.
proposed: Keep the request as a REST call inside a CaseWorkflow activity, which fills the E cell as a consumer of the P6 answer and replaces the legacy in-process call with one hop; if the architecture review prefers an event-only exchange, the activity becomes a signal and the case reads the answer through the notice read without changing the case-side writes.

title: The per-service login name and the case-side feature switch key are not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 DP-02 and DP-06; legacy RWB-E1-052 section 13 (feature flag rwb.comms.notice-generation); TSD P3 v3 T6.1 and T6.2
description: The story names the rwb-case service identity and a case-side parameter that switches the notice request off. No source gives a login name for the service and none names the case-side parameter key or its default; the legacy flag belongs to the generating service.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T6.1 and T6.2 name the service roles SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES but no login string; the legacy flag rwb.comms.notice-generation is a P6 flag and stays there.
proposed: Name the login in the platform DB story that gives one login per service, and load the case-side switch as a parameter through the parameters contract with a default of on, owned by RW-COE.

title: The platform contract dependencies of the pattern table are not carried in the metadata rows
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table and R7.1; WP B-P3-09 story line for RWB-P3-E1052-APP (H empty, C RWB-P6-E1052-CON)
description: The DP table adds platform contract dependencies for DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19, while the metadata rows of the work package carry no build dependency and a single contract dependency. The story therefore applies the DP patterns and names the platform contract stories in the pattern table and in the preconditions, and the metadata rows carry the contract dependency of this legacy key.
evidence: The work package line for RWB-P3-E1052-APP has H empty; the DP rows add H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
proposed: Keep the metadata rows as the work package gives them and hold the platform contract dependencies in the pattern table and in the preconditions, so that the lane stays Day 1 and the platform stories are not duplicated in the story metadata.

title: Review team for a review item with no case: the legacy value is assumed and the parameter has no agreed owner
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 054 Review queue for low confidence documents v1.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md
section: Preconditions; legacy BR2; section 8 BR3 and section 13 of this story
description: The legacy story names REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED with the value DOC-SVC marked assumed, while its own AC background sets the value to LIT-BKK for the test, and the parameter row lives in document_hub_parameter, a P5 table. The rwb-case review queue must route an item without a case to that team and reads the value through the parameters and reference contracts of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), so the owner, the key and the production value are open.
evidence: Legacy story section 3 lists REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED value DOC-SVC as assumed; legacy AC background sets REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED to LIT-BKK for this test; the ownership map gives document_hub_parameter to P5.
proposed: Keep the key as a data row loaded through the parameters contract of rwb-case, with the review team of each environment agreed by RW-COE, and let P5 keep its own row for its screen; the queue reads the rwb-case row only.

title: The rwb-case feature switch of the review queue has no name in any source
source: Legacy RWB-E1-054 section 13; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling on feature flags
description: The legacy flag rwb.dochub.review stays with rwb-document. The rwb-case switch that stops a review task being raised is named by no source, and feature flags are platform objects under the R-PREC default ruling while this story needs a parameter read through the parameters contract.
evidence: Legacy story section 13 names only the flag rwb.dochub.review; no source names a rwb-case review switch.
proposed: Load the switch as a parameter through the parameters contract, stored in the platform flag library; off means no review task is raised and the review queue answers no row.

title: The review task code, the review state values, the case-side decision code and the field IDs of the review link columns are not specified
source: TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.1 and T3.2; Legacy RWB-E1-054
description: TSD P3 v3 gives task_code, owner_role, status and outcome_code but no review task code, no review state vocabulary and no decision code for a case-side review record, and the four review link columns this story adds to task (document_ref, review_reason, item_version, review_state) have no field IDs.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 task DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026; T3.2 LOV-TASK-STATUS; no list holds a review task code, a review state or a review decision code.
proposed: Load the task code, the review states and the decision code as reference rows through the reference-data contract, and allocate field IDs for the four link columns at the next data dictionary version.

title: The rwb-case per-service login name is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41
description: DP-02 requires one login per service and Architecture v5 names the schema rwb_case, but no source gives the login name of rwb-case.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives schema rwb_case with its own login and no name; DP-02 states one login per service.
proposed: Agree the login name with the platform DB story RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and use it for the grants, the Flyway history and the connection pool of rwb-case.

title: The holiday calendar read on the rwb-source-data contract has no named operation
source: Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5, TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (T3.1 line 15 v_ace_holiday over bot_holiday; T-A.1 API-P1-001 to API-P1-016); Functional Specifications by Module v6, FSD P1 v3 (holiday calendar REUSE, read through v_ace_holiday)
section: Contract / 12.2 REST operations consumed; Solution plan / DueDateCalculator
description: Legacy RWB-E1-045 BR7 reads the public holidays of a working-day period from the v_ace_holiday view. DP-05 moves every ACE view read behind the rwb-source-data contract, but no P1 source names the operation that returns the holidays of a date range, and no P1 endpoint in the appendix covers holidays. The story therefore cites the read as a contract operation inside the CalculateDueDate activity without an operation name or path.
evidence: TSD P1 v3 T3.1 line 15 and T-A.1 (no holiday endpoint between API-P1-001 and API-P1-016); FSD P1 v3 'Holiday calendar REUSE v_ace_holiday'; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 45 'Who reads ACE's data?'
proposed: rwb-source-data publishes one holiday calendar read (a Temporal activity or a GET on the source-data base path) returning the holiday dates of a date range; rwb-case consumes it inside CalculateDueDate and reads no ACE view

title: The required service-level status list is not in the target sources
source: Legacy RWB-E1-045 section 8 BR3 and section 13 (assumed list, DL22); FSD P3 v4 A2.11 and A2.25; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-CASE-STATUS
section: Business rules / BR3; Configuration and reference data
description: BR3 requires one SERVICE_LEVEL row per status in the parameter servicelevel.required-statuses. The legacy story lists six statuses as an assumption and no current FSD, TSD or BRD gives the parameter value or confirms the list, so the completeness check of AC3 cannot be proved against a sourced list.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-045 BR3 '(assumed NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, WAITING_PARTNER, WAITING_APPROVAL; DL22)' and section 13 'assumed list in BR3'; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-CASE-STATUS (NEW, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_CUSTOMER, WAITING_PARTNER, WAITING_APPROVAL, ON_HOLD, CLOSED); FSD P3 v4 A2.11.3.1 and A2.25.3.1
proposed: Keep the legacy assumed list of six statuses as the parameter default and confirm it with the service-level owner before the first SERVICE_LEVEL load; ON_HOLD and CLOSED stay outside the list unless the owner adds them

title: The classification answer the case needs is not carried by the published document contract or by EV-16 and EV-17
source: API Specification v4 (Document schema; DocumentChecklist schema); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 42 (EV-16, EV-17); Event and Messaging Design v4; RWB-P5-E1050-APP fragment (events_published)
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.4 Events consumed; 12.8 Contract fakes; 15 Screens and states
description: rwb-case must apply the document type code, the classifier version, the confidence, the review reason and the two candidate types that rwb-document produced. The published Document schema carries documentType, classificationConfidence and reviewStatus only; the DocumentChecklist schema carries the checklist version and the items with documentType, label, required and presentCount; the EV-16 payload is documentId, caseId, type and source and the EV-17 payload is documentId, fields and confidence. None of them carries classifierVersion, reviewReason or the two candidates with their confidence, and the P5 slice of this legacy key publishes rwb.document.DocumentClassified.v1, an event the Architecture v5 catalogue does not name.
evidence: API Specification v4 components.schemas.Document properties id, caseId, personKey, documentType, source, storageRef, classificationConfidence, reviewStatus, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion, previousVersionId, contentSha256; DocumentChecklist properties caseId, checklistVersion, stageCode, items, missingCount, complete; ChecklistItem properties documentType, label, required, presentCount; Event and Messaging Design v4 rows EV-16 and EV-17; fragments/RWB-P5-E1050-APP.json events_published [rwb.document.DocumentClassified.v1].
proposed: Extend the rwb-document published contract and the EV-16 payload with classifierVersion, reviewReason, candidateOneType with its confidence and candidateTwoType with its confidence, or add one agreed classified event to the Architecture v5 catalogue and consume that; the story builds against the extended contract and its fake until the contract story is raised.

title: The rwb-case login name is not in the sources
source: TSD P3 v3 T2.5 and T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 note
description: The sources name the service identity of every workflow and the service login pattern, but no source states the login name of rwb-case. The story needs it for the schema owner, the contract reader and the Schedule owner.
evidence: TSD P3 v3 T2.5 names the worker identity SY-CASEWF and the evaluator identity SY-RULES only; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the schema rwb_case and the task queue rwb-case, not a login; DP-02 gives one login per service without a naming rule.
proposed: Agree the rwb-case login with the ACE DB team under DP-02 and record it in the service catalogue; the story names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until then.

title: The texts of MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-GEN-006 are not in the source extracts
source: FSD P3 v4 A2.10 and A2.45 exception flows; FSD P1 v3 A2.17; FSD P6 v3 A2.7; FSD P4 v3 A2.7
section: 5 Exception paths; 12.1 REST operations provided; 14 Validation and messages
description: Both messages are cited by ID in the specifications but their text is not in any extract available to this story. MSG-GEN-004 is used for a second request that cannot be taken at the same time (409) and MSG-GEN-006 for a source service that does not answer, but the wording is not given.
evidence: FSD P3 v4 A2.10 alternate flow: the second transfer is refused with MSG-GEN-004; FSD P4 v3 A2.7: the call returns status 409 with message MSG-GEN-004; FSD P1 v3 A2.15 and FSD P3 v4 A2.45: a source that does not answer raises MSG-GEN-006 naming the service; no extract holds the message table.
proposed: Read both texts from the message catalogue at build time and keep the IDs in this story unchanged; Thai text follows DL10.

title: No source names a classifier version label or its format
source: Legacy RWB-E1-050 sections 3, 4 and 11; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-DOC-073
description: The legacy story says the model version of the classifier is known and writes it as classifier_version, but no source gives a version label, a length beyond the 40 characters of the document-side column, or a naming rule. The story stores the value as received and needs a fixture for its tests.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-050 section 3: "its model version is known"; section 4 step 5 writes classifier_version; LDM v8 DF-DOC-073 document_intake.classifier_version varchar(40) with no format; no extract names a version label.
proposed: Treat the classifier version as an opaque string of up to 40 characters exactly as rwb-document returns it, and use the synthetic fixture TEST-CLF-0007 in every test; no format is imposed by rwb-case.

title: The case document link is not an Owner row and has no field IDs
source: Ownership Map v1 (document, document_checklist_item, case_document_check all P5); TSD P3 v3 T3.1; Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: 11 Data; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Database and migrations
description: rwb-case holds the case-side link, its checklist item state and the classification columns, but the Ownership Map gives no rwb_case link table and the Logical Data Model gives no field IDs for one. The table is created by RWB-P3-E1032-APP and this story adds the classification columns to it.
evidence: Ownership Map tables: document P5, document_checklist_item P5, case_document_check P5; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 lists recovery_case, case_account, case_party, queue, assignment, task, timer, interaction, case_entry_exclusion and the reference and parameter tables only; LDM v8 has no case-side link table.
proposed: Add the classification columns to rwb_case.case_document_link in V1050_1 and register the table with its field IDs in the next data dictionary version; rwb-case writes no P5 table.

title: The rwb-case switch key and the re-drive time of day are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-050 sections 3 and 13; Template and Rules v1 DP-06 and DP-10; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44
section: 12.6 Schedules; 13 Configuration and reference data; 13 Feature switch
description: The legacy flag rwb.dochub.classify belongs to the document hub and stays there. rwb-case needs its own switch, read as a parameter, and the daily re-drive Schedule needs a time of day; no source gives either value.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-050 section 3 and section 13 name rwb.dochub.classify only; DP-06 puts parameters in the rwb-case parameters contract without naming keys; Architecture v5 slide 44 has no job for a classification re-drive in rwb-case.
proposed: Agree one boolean parameter key for the rwb-case classification handler with RW-COE and set the daily re-drive outside the case-creation and allocation windows; both are data and need no code change.

title: The decision record is written here although DP-03 and its library story are not applied
source: Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-03; WP B-P3-09 story line (patterns without DP03, H empty); Ownership Map (decision_log_entry P7)
section: 8 Business rules; 11 Data; 12.3 Events published; 13 Solution plan
description: The story must write a decision record for every applied classification, but DP-03 is not among its patterns and the WP records no build dependency on the decision-record library. The central ledger table decision_log_entry is owned by P7, so the write can only be the local decision-record table created in rwb_case.
evidence: WP B-P3-09 story line for RWB-P3-E1050-APP: patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP10, DP11, DP15, DP19; H [] and C []; Ownership Map decision_log_entry owner P7; Template and Rules v1 DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.
proposed: Write the decision record as a local row in the rwb_case decision-record table created by the service baseline, publish no DecisionRecorded event and claim no platform dependency; if the ledger is required for a document decision, DP-03 and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON are added to this story.

title: Gap cited in B-P3-09
description: Cited by _work/msr/editlog/B-P3-09.md; see the story body for the missing value.
source: _work/msr/editlog/B-P3-09.md
evidence: Citation in a Stage B output
proposed: Confirm during the verification loop
